The user, 2026-11-15: "I want an alternating 5v5v5 run of vanilla 1.15.1 vs No Free Upgrades 1.1.1 vs PMR's latest version", then "n=5 might not be enough. Let's have it this way: n=15 PMR vs 5 vanilla vs 5 NFU. Wall clock speed comparisons are in-session only, but for measurements the latest vanilla vs NFU batch goes glued to this batch's results." _predictions._note: The agent's, written before any PMR run. Directions are argued; no magnitude is.
_predictions.world_gdp: PMR ends below vanilla: a new recipe costs half a level's construction per level, where vanilla switches free, and that construction competes with new levels. Expected 0.80-1.00x vanilla at the end, with the gap widest mid-century.
_predictions.majors_gdp: The technology leaders (Britain, Germany, the USA, France) lose more against vanilla than the periphery, because they hold the most recipes to retool to.
_predictions.depeasantation: World U* at or slightly above vanilla's (construction spent on retooling creates no new jobs), far below the canon's gap to vanilla; the shortlist stays near full employment as in vanilla.
_predictions.hoarding: The investment pool / GDP at or below vanilla's: retooling is one more thing for private investors to buy.
_predictions.play_time: PMR slower than vanilla (its page: a monthly script runs per building) and slower than the canon; magnitude unknown, the reason for the 540-minute timeout on its runs.
_predictions.ai_government: Unknown, and a thing to read: whether AI governments retool the levels they own. If they do not, government-owned industry stays on its starting recipes for the century.

_stop_rule: None: a fixed-n batch plays every run (no stop watcher, no deadline).
